description: Shandalar is a plane that is abnormally rich in mana, home to Thune's mountain border, the Onakke spirits and, later, Tam.

timeline.summary: Trapped in the Shard during the Ice Age, Leshrac summons an elder dragon against Kristina of the Woods and plans to conquer Shandalar with Tevesh Szat.
timeline.quote: He wanted to conquer that mana -rich plane , and allied with Tevesh Szat to achieve this.

citation.text: "Leshrac", section "The Ice Age". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leshrac escapes to Shandalar and starts the War for Shandalar, but without his undead host he is defeated by Kenan Sahrmal.
timeline.quote: he was defeated by Kenan Sahrmal

citation.text: "Leshrac", section "The Ice Age". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: During the time of the Shard of the Twelve Worlds, Faralyn, Tevesh Szat, Leshrac and Lim-Dûl invade Shandalar.
timeline.quote: They immediately began to wage war upon the plane, ready to claim it for their own.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Sahrmal". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Sahrmal kills Faralyn with a summoned astral dragon and routs the others; Lim-Dûl injures Sahrmal, and Sahrmal's followers behead Lim-Dûl.
timeline.quote: managed to kill Faralyn with a summoned astral dragon

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Sahrmal". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Freyalise uses Shandalar's wandering to cast the World Spell on Dominaria, ending the Ice Age and shattering the Shard.
timeline.quote: the unique wandering of Shandalar was used by Freyalise to cast the World Spell ending that plane's Ice Age and shattering the Shard.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Sahrmal". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Sahrmal invests his remaining power in his other apprentice, who becomes the Guardian, and vanishes again.
timeline.quote: Sahrmal's pupil became known as The Guardian and took up the role of Protector of Shandalar.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "The Guardian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Guardian establishes five guilds of magic, each teaching one color of mana.
timeline.quote: The Guardian established five guilds of magic

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "The Guardian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In the Wizards' War the five wizard schools resist Lim-Dûl, who is defeated; the Guardian imprisons his soul in an artifact.
timeline.quote: The Guardian removed Lim-Dûl's soul from Azar's body and imprisoned it within a magical artifact

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "The Wizards' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Azar's empty body rises and becomes Lichlord Skavius Slan, ruling the Black Guild.
timeline.quote: it rose on its own and took the name Lichlord Skavius Slan .

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "The Wizards' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Manipulated by Arzakon, the Guildlords rise up and strike down the Guardian.
timeline.quote: rose and struck down the Guardian.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Arzakon". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Arzakon tricks the Guildlords into seeking the Spell of Dominion, really meant to destroy the artifact that sustains the Great Barrier.
timeline.quote: Of course, this was untrue.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Arzakon". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kenan Sahrmal defends Shandalar, but Lim-Dûl is beheaded by Sahrmal's followers and survives by moving his soul to another body.
timeline.quote: Lim-Dûl had survived by transferring his soul into another body

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "War for Shandalar". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Twelve years later Lim-Dûl returns with an undead army and destroys city after city on Shandalar until only Ardestan remains.
timeline.quote: only one city remained: Ardestan

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "Lim-Dûl's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Azar casts a spell to imprison Lim-Dûl's spirit and create the Great Barrier, but both spirits become trapped in Azar's body.
timeline.quote: The combined spells had the unforeseen effect of trapping both spirits within Azar’s body.

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "Lim-Dûl's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Azar falls and Lim-Dûl resumes his campaign, but is finally defeated in the Wizard's War and his soul imprisoned in the Chain Veil.
timeline.quote: imprisoned it within the Chain Veil , a magical artifact that kept the Great Barrier intact

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "Lim-Dûl's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Arzakon tricks the guild masters into casting the Spell of Dominion, meant to destroy the Chain Veil, but is thwarted.
timeline.quote: Arzakon's plans were thwarted, and both he and the guild lords were defeated by one of the plane's spellcasters

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "Arzakon's War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lim-Dûl and two planeswalkers escape imprisonment in the Shard and arrive on Shandalar; Sahrmal drives off all but Lim-Dûl, who stabs the weakened hero with a pitchfork before the followers behead him.
timeline.quote: The necromancer chose the aftermath of that battle as an advantageous moment to pierce Kenan Sahrmal with a pitchfork.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Preface". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Twelve years later Lim-Dûl returns with an undead army and wages a years-long war that destroys every major city but one.
timeline.quote: Lim-Dûl reappeared with an army of the undead at his side and attempted to seize dominion over the entire plane.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Lim-Dûl’s return". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Sahrmal, nearly powerless, secretly trains two adepts, Azaar and a nameless one, to defeat Lim-Dûl.
timeline.quote: Shandalar’s hero had been secretly training two adepts to take his place.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Lim-Dûl’s return". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Sahrmal invests his remaining power in his second pupil, making him immortal, names him his replacement, vows to stay out of events and vanishes.
timeline.quote: Sahrmal named the nameless wizard as his replacement, took a vow to never again take an active part in events in Shandalar, then vanished.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The Guardian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The new wizard declares himself The Guardian, immortal protector of Shandalar.
timeline.quote: I am The Guardian

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The Guardian". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Guardian establishes five guilds, one for each color, whose first leaders are chosen in a great contest and become Guild Lords.
timeline.quote: he established five guilds, one focused on each color of magic

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The Wizards' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: In the Wizards' War Lim-Dûl's spirit, having won over Azaar's, emerges to conquer Shandalar but is defeated; the Guardian imprisons him in an artifact.
timeline.quote: In the great Wizards' War , Lim-Dûl was defeated soundly, though the Lord of the Black Guild also fell.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The Wizards' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Azaar's emptied body rises as the undead Lichlord Skavius Sian and takes command of the Black Guild, while the Guardian hides the artifact.
timeline.quote: it rose of its own accord and stepped in to command the Black Guild, taking the name Lichlord Skavius Sian

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The Wizards' War". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Arzakon traces the magical ripples to Shandalar and tries to penetrate the Great Barrier, but the Guardian repels it.
timeline.quote: the Guardian lent strength to the barrier and easily repelled Arzakon ’s physical intrusion

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Azarkon". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: At a conclave the five Guild Lords, manipulated by Arzakon, rise as one and strike down the Guardian.
timeline.quote: rose suddenly as one and struck down the Guardian

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Revolt of the Guild Lords". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Arzakon sets the Guild Lords a race to cast the Spell of Dominion, and their minions scour Shandalar seizing magical resources.
timeline.quote: Arzakon laid a task and a challenge before them.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Revolt of the Guild Lords". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: An elderly oneiromancer divines that Arzakon wants to conquer Shandalar itself and that the Spell of Dominion would destroy the artifact and shatter the barrier.
timeline.quote: Arzakon intends to conquer Shandalar himself.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The novice". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The oneiromancer convinces a wandering novice spellcaster, to whom the Guardian speaks briefly, making the novice Shandalar's last hope.
timeline.quote: Now, that lone figure is all that stands between Shandalar and its doom.

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "The novice". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Great Barrier fails, the Guilds fall, and new nations rise; Ob Nixilis comes for the Chain Veil and is cursed.
timeline.quote: At some point, Ob Nixilis came for the Chain Veil and was cursed by its power.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Fall of the guilds". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Faralyn arrives on Shandalar from the Shard, mocks Tevesh Szat, Leshrac and Lim-Dûl, and claims the plane for himself.
timeline.quote: He mocks them for trying to betray him and claims Shandalar for his own.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 1: Exiles In The Promised Land". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: An Astral dragon feeds Faralyn mana until he can bear no more and explodes in a rainbow of colors.
timeline.quote: It fills Faralyn with mana until the wizards can't take it anymore and explodes in a rainbow of colors.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 1: Exiles In The Promised Land". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leshrac, watching Faralyn's end, wards himself against other planeswalkers and vows to defeat Sahrmal and conquer Shandalar.
timeline.quote: He vows to defeat Kenan Sahrmal and conquer Shandalar for his own.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 1: Exiles In The Promised Land". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Szat reflects on Dominaria and his sister, blaming himself for Tymolin's death.
timeline.quote: all pleasure perished when he let Tymolin die

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 1: Exiles In The Promised Land". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Bani and her allies fight Tevesh Szat, now calling himself World-Ender, in the desert while Sahrmal watches in astral form.
timeline.quote: who now calls himself World-Ender

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 2: The Threshold". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lim-Dûl plots to trick Sahrmal into attacking the planeswalkers, creates Manabarbs against Szat; Sahrmal joins with Fire Sprites, Szat devours Anthanor and casts Winter's Chill.
timeline.quote: The spell completely devours the soldier.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 2: The Threshold". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Sahrmal reveals his mortal form and protects Bani, but Szat stuns him with Infernal Darkness.
timeline.quote: This is the moment that Sahrmal unveils his mortal form.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 2: The Threshold". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Leshrac returns and tells Szat that Lim-Dûl is sapping him with manabarbs; the bickering planeswalkers retreat as Sahrmal casts Whimsy.
timeline.quote: Disgusted and frustrated with Shandalar's bizarre mana, Szat and Leshrac make a hasty retreat.

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 2: The Threshold". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Lim-Dûl swaps bodies with Sahrmal using Mirror Universe, and Bani beheads Sahrmal's body while Lim-Dûl's essence in Sahrmal's body fades away.
timeline.quote: enough to allow Bani to slice off his head

citation.text: "Shandalar (comic)", section "Volume 2: The Threshold". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana Vess takes control of the Chain Veil on Shandalar.
timeline.quote: Liliana Vess takes control of the Chain Veil on Shandalar .

citation.text: "Timeline", section "The Mending Era (4500 AR to 4562 AR)". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Kothophed sends Liliana to find the Chain Veil on Shandalar.
timeline.quote: Kothophed gave Liliana the task of searching for an ancient and powerful relic known as the Chain Veil

citation.text: "Liliana Vess", section "The Hunter and the Veil". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The veil-enhanced Liliana dispatches Garruk in the Onakke temple.
timeline.quote: Garruk attacked her in the temple after she had located the veil and tracked her through the hidden tunnels until he was dispatched by the veil-enhanced Liliana.

citation.text: "Liliana Vess", section "The Hunter and the Veil". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garruk's spark ignites and he planeswalks for the first time, to Shandalar.
timeline.quote: his first planeswalk was to Shandalar

citation.text: "Garruk", section "Early life". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Garruk hunts the Ursoth, then rages at Liliana for killing one of his beasts and assaults her in an Onakke temple.
timeline.quote: he flew into a rage and tracked her down, assaulting her in an ancient Onakke temple

citation.text: "Garruk", section "The Hunter, the Veil, and The Veil's Curse". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana uses the Chain Veil to overpower and curse Garruk.
timeline.quote: Liliana overpowered him with a surge of black magic that cursed him

citation.text: "Garruk", section "The Hunter, the Veil, and The Veil's Curse". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana retrieves the Chain Veil from the Shandalar catacombs as instructed by Kothophed, then uses it to destroy Kothophed and Griselbrand and pass the demon curse to Garruk.
timeline.quote: retrieved the Chain Veil from the catacombs at Shandalar

citation.text: "Chain Veil", section "History". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Jace halts Garruk's chain veil curse by implanting a hedron in him.
timeline.quote: Jace succeeded in implanting the hedron in Garruk and halting the curse of the chain veil.

citation.text: "Jace Beleren", section "Unfinished Business". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana arrives on Shandalar, tormented by the Chain Veil's voices, and heads for the Onakke catacomb she has visited before.
timeline.quote: all she could hear was the veil.

citation.text: "Veil of Deceit" by James Wyatt. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 1 Jul 2014.

timeline.summary: Liliana recalls using the Chain Veil to kill her demon patron Kothophed and then Griselbrand, and her earlier ill-fated visit to learn of the Onakke.
timeline.quote: Instead of bringing it back to him like a good little retriever, she'd used its power to kill him.

citation.text: "Veil of Deceit" by James Wyatt. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 1 Jul 2014.

timeline.summary: Liliana recalls her first visit, when she killed her horse's attacker and used the veil to infect Garruk with shadow, after which he hunted her to Innistrad.
timeline.quote: She'd used it to infect him with shadow, polluting his nature magic with the touch of death.

citation.text: "Veil of Deceit" by James Wyatt. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 1 Jul 2014.

timeline.summary: A suppression Hedron stops Garruk's transformation into the Worldslayer demon in the Onakke Catacomb.
timeline.quote: a suppression Hedron was used to stop Garruk's transformation into a demon

citation.text: "Garruk", section "Apex predator". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Jace appears to Garruk disguised as Liliana; the ruse fails and Garruk warns him off.
timeline.quote: Masking himself as Liliana, Jace once more appeared before Garruk.

citation.text: "Garruk", section "Apex predator". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana stabs the Raven Man.
timeline.quote: Aware now of the being she had been speaking to, she stabbed him.

citation.text: "Liliana Vess", section "The Raven's Eye". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana kills the angel guarding the Onakke Temple.
timeline.quote: Ignoring the angel's pleas and warnings, Liliana killed her.

citation.text: "Liliana Vess", section "Echoes of the Past". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana dissipates an Onakke ghost with the veil's power.
timeline.quote: Liliana drew on the veil's power and dissipated the ghost.

citation.text: "Liliana Vess", section "Echoes of the Past". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: The Raven Man orchestrates Liliana's discovery of the Chain Veil on Shandalar.
timeline.quote: A while later, the Raven Man orchestrated Liliana's discovery of the Chain Veil on Shandalar .

citation.text: "Lim-Dûl", section "Haunting Liliana Vess". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Liliana recalls using the Chain Veil to kill Kothophed and Griselbrand and being unable to leave it behind.
timeline.quote: It was bound to her, and her to it.

citation.text: "Unkindness of Ravens" by James Wyatt. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 29 Jul 2015.

timeline.summary: During the Phyrexian invasion, the Chain Veil's magic empowers the Onakke, and wild mana shreds compleated Phyrexians' augmentations.
timeline.quote: Compleated Phyrexians on the plane found their metallic augmentations shredded by the pervasive wild magic of the plane's mana.

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "Phyrexian invasion". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

timeline.summary: Ajani refuses to take Liliana along and plans to reach the students through a stable Omenpath between Lorwyn and Shandalar.
timeline.quote: I can't take you with me.

citation.work: Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 3: Aweary of This Moon
citation.text: "Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 3: Aweary of This Moon" by Seanan McGuire. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 10 Dec 2025.

timeline.summary: Ajani leads the group through an Omenpath to Shandalar and on to Arcavios, bringing Lluwen.
timeline.quote: Together, they walked into the cascading light, and another world was left behind.

citation.work: Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 7: The Charm Dissolves Apace
citation.text: "Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 7: The Charm Dissolves Apace" by Seanan McGuire. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 16 Dec 2025.

timeline.summary: The inhabitants of Shandalar must combat the growing hive mind of the slivers, which threatens to consume their world.
timeline.quote: Now the inhabitants of this unusual plane must combat the growing hive mind of the slivers

citation.text: "Shandalar". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

relations.note: The border of Thune lies in the mountains of Shandalar.
relations.quote: the mountains at the border of Thune in Shandalar

citation.text: "Xathrid Gorgon" by Jenna Helland. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 3 Jul 2012.

citation.text: "Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 3: Aweary of This Moon" by Seanan McGuire. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 10 Dec 2025.

relations.note: Tam and Alandra are from Shandalar.
relations.quote: Tam and your classmate Alandra are from there

citation.work: Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 7: The Charm Dissolves Apace
citation.text: "Lorwyn Eclipsed | Episode 7: The Charm Dissolves Apace" by Seanan McGuire. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 16 Dec 2025.

relations.quote: hidden within the ancient catacombs of the Onakke at Shandalar

citation.text: "Chain Veil". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

relations.quote: A planeswalker who chose to preserve rather than prey on his home plane

citation.text: "Magic: The Gathering (MicroProse)/Backstory", section "Preface". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

relations.quote: an ever-evolving race that threatens to consume their world.

citation.text: "Shandalar". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

relations.quote: It was once home to the Onakke, an ogre civilization

citation.text: "Shandalar". Magic: The Gathering story profiles, Wizards of the Coast.

relations.quote: The Veil itself is an artifact hidden within the catacombs of the Onakke

citation.text: "Shandalar", section "The Onakke". MTG Wiki contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, MTG Wiki contributors.

pages_say.description: A mana-rich plane with no fixed location, wandering through the Blind Eternities.

citation.text: "The Planes of Planechase". Savor the Flavor, Wizards of the Coast, 31 Aug 2009. Archived by the Internet Archive.

pages_say.description: A vast plane containing Thune and the eastern lands.

citation.text: "Xathrid Gorgon" by Jenna Helland. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 3 Jul 2012.

pages_say.description: A plane whose name matches one of the victims.

citation.text: "The Gorgon and the Guildpact" by Doug Beyer. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 12 Mar 2014.

pages_say.description: The plane where the Chain Veil and the Onakke catacomb are found.

citation.text: "Veil of Deceit" by James Wyatt. Magic Story, Wizards of the Coast, 1 Jul 2014.
